title: Proton pump inhibitors for the prevention of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug-induced ulcers and dyspepsia
authors: Garegnani L, Oltra G, Burgos MA, Ivaldi D, Varela LB, Díaz Menai S, et al.
followUp: up to 12 months; most trials about 6 months
population: 12 randomised trials published 1996 to 2014 in outpatients taking NSAIDs for 4 weeks or longer; PPI against placebo, H2-receptor antagonist or misoprostol; pharmaceutical companies funded 7 of the 12 trials
funder: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.
authorConflicts: One author worked as biostatistics consultant for the Instituto Ecuatoriano de Enfermedades Digestivas; others none relevant.
result: PPI against placebo: incident ulcers 36 against 119 per 1000 (RR 0.29, 95% CI 0.23 to 0.36; 11 trials, 7022 participants; moderate certainty); ulcer complications 4 against 11 per 1000 (RR 0.33, 0.10 to 1.07; 5 trials, 4394 participants; low certainty); global dyspepsia symptoms little or no effect (very low certainty); adverse events could not be pooled (very low certainty). PPI against H2-receptor antagonist: 154 against 77 ulcers per 1000 (1 trial, 26 participants). PPI against misoprostol: more ulcers (RR 2.32, 1.25 to 4.30) and fewer adverse events (RR 0.38, 0.25 to 0.57; 1 trial, 402 participants; very low certainty).
